solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One looking for clues left in houses?

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for left is placed within the word for houses

parts.note: houses are homes

explanation.surface: A detective is asked where he searches: perhaps somewhere left in houses?
explanation.walkthrough: Sherlock Holmes is the fictional detective, the archetypal clue-seeker.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherlock, the fictional detective, spends his stories hunting for clues.

clue.text: Old volunteers work in region of South Island

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
to go is to work or function, as a machine does

explanation.surface: Retired reservists find employment in a part of New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer reserve. 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is a province occupying the south-east of New Zealand's South Island.

clue.text: Clumsy matador, I will get twisted round bull's tail

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
twisted letters are bent out of their order, so the matador and I are rearranged
the tail of a word is its final letter, here of bull

explanation.surface: An inept bullfighter is warned he'll be tossed about by the animal's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will get twisted' rearranges the matador and I; 'round' wraps that around the last letter of bull, so L sits third.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit is a formal synonym for clumsy or awkward.

clue.text: Put off the woman — darling not to have ring

parts.note: she is the pronoun for the woman

indicators.note: not to have something means dropping it, so the ring shape goes from the word for darling

parts.note: love is a term of endearment like darling
O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: A woman postpones things because her sweetheart lacks an engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to have' removes O (a ring shape) from LOVE, leaving LVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelve a plan is to postpone or defer it.

clue.text: Funny play deficient, now sadly a disappointment

indicators.note: deficient means lacking, here lacking its final letter

parts.note: a comedy is a funny play

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of now are jumbled

explanation.surface: A theatre critic finds a comic play lacking and is now let down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deficient' cuts the last letter from COMEDY, leaving COMED; 'sadly' turns NOW into OWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedown is a letdown, a fall from expectations.

clue.text: Come in to pal's, say, after accident, showing sympathy

indicators.note: after an accident things are wrecked, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of pal's without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A friend is invited round, perhaps after a crash, to receive some comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses every letter of COME IN TO PALS SAY, fifteen in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting compassionately means acting with sympathy and tender concern.

clue.text: Finish with blame flying around — not going to scrap yet?

indicators.note: around says the jumbled letters go round the word for finish
flying letters are scattered about, so blame is rearranged

parts.note: an end is a finish

explanation.surface: Someone ends an argument with accusations flying, though the item isn't yet for the scrapheap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' jumbles blame into MABLE, and 'around' wraps it about the finish word. The definition is a cryptic hint at something worth repairing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repairable is fit to be fixed rather than thrown away as scrap.

clue.text: What Euclid saw as a triangle?

definitions.text: What Euclid saw as a triangle?

parts.words: What Euclid saw as a triangle?
parts.note: a Greek geometer would see a triangle shape as one of his own alphabet's letters, the fourth one

explanation.walkthrough: The capital form of the fourth Greek letter is drawn as a triangle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek capital letter for D is shaped like a triangle, which Euclid would read as a letter.

clue.text: Feeble report of Sunday-to-Saturday requirement

indicators.note: a report is something heard, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: a week runs Sunday to Saturday, so this is a week need

explanation.surface: A weak argument is presented about what a whole week demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report of' signals a homophone: 'week need' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak-kneed means lacking resolve or courage, so feeble.

clue.text: Actor's headline portrayal of Saul's conversion

definitions.text: Actor's headline portrayal of Saul's conversion

parts.words: Actor's headline portrayal of Saul's conversion
parts.note: on the Damascus road Saul took the name of the apostle and became a different, reborn person, which names a Hollywood star

explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible, Saul of Tarsus converted, was called Paul, and became a 'new man'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollywood star's name combines the apostle's new name with the idea of a reborn person.

clue.text: Something on meal table in lounge

definitions.meaning: a bread item put out at mealtimes
to lounge is to idle or lie about lazily

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A loaf of bread sits on the table; to loaf is to lounge around idly.

clue.text: Mum carrying antique through part of Europe

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the word for mum holds the word for antique

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum
antique means old
via means by way of, through

explanation.surface: A mother lugs a heirloom across a stretch of the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts the antique word inside the mum word; Moldavia is the older name for the Moldova region.
explanation.definitionFit: Moldavia is the historic name for the region of eastern Europe now largely Moldova.

clue.text: State unfortunately having a king overthrown

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of regret, unfortunately

indicators.note: overthrown means turned over, so these letters are read backwards in this down-the-page sense

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A nation regrets that its monarch has been deposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrown' turns A K into KA after ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is the largest US state.

clue.text: A female runs round for a hairdo

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A woman dashes around town looking for a hairdresser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; R for runs comes from cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, bushy hairstyle.

clue.text: Severe bodily condition — what could be best for it?

indicators.note: could be suggests these letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical question asks which treatment would suit a serious ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what could be' asks for the anagram of BEST FOR IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Frostbite is serious tissue damage caused by freezing.

clue.text: Writer in South Africa having to hang around

parts.note: to linger is to hang around

explanation.surface: An author living in South Africa is obliged to stay on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'having to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: J D Salinger was the American author of The Catcher in the Rye.

clue.text: City that may be built when the incoming waves have been destructive?

definitions.text: City that may be built when the incoming waves have been destructive?

parts.words: City that may be built when the incoming waves have been destructive?
parts.note: after the tide knocks down your sandcastle on the beach, you build a fresh one, naming an English city

explanation.walkthrough: Read the city as 'new castle': a replacement sandcastle once the tide has wrecked the old one.
explanation.definitionFit: This northern English city on the Tyne also reads as a fresh fortress.

clue.text: Smart, having washed wound?

definitions.meaning: read literally, an injury that has been cleaned

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical literal reading of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean-cut means neat and wholesome-looking, so smart; literally it is a cleaned gash.

clue.text: Elvis in huge theatre initially drowned by instrument

indicators.note: drowned by means swamped, enclosed by the instrument word

parts.note: a cello is a stringed instrument
OS stands for outsize, meaning huge

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of theatre is taken

explanation.surface: A singer at a vast venue is overwhelmed at first by the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: Elvis Costello is the British singer-songwriter. OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize; 'drowned by' sinks that and T into the instrument after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Costello is a famous British singer, so the first name points to the surname.

clue.text: Former tennis champ put on the scales, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: something put on the scales has been weighed

explanation.surface: A retired tennis star steps on the scales.
explanation.walkthrough: Virginia Wade won Wimbledon in 1977.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Wade is a British former Wimbledon singles winner.

clue.text: Look towards the setting sun, being most depressed

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
the sun sets in the west

explanation.surface: Someone gazes at the sunset while feeling at their lowest ebb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowest is the superlative of low, meaning most dejected.

clue.text: University better than the others, one having a wonderful situation

parts.note: top means best of all
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A university claims to be superior, each student enjoying an ideal place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link word; the final A is the clue's own 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is an imagined perfect place or state of affairs.

clue.text: King and his son maybe half cut before noon

indicators.note: cutting half the word leaves its first three letters

parts.note: a king's son is a prince
AM means before noon

explanation.surface: A monarch and his heir, somewhat drunk, before lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' (British slang for tipsy) drops NCE from PRINCE, leaving PRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the King of Troy in Greek legend.

clue.text: A maiden and friend hoarding gold with no concern for ethical values

definitions.text: with no concern for ethical values

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
or is gold in heraldry
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A girl and her companion stash gold, untroubled by morality.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold; M for maiden is a cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting amorally means acting without any sense of right and wrong.

clue.text: Woman in peril, in danger

indicators.note: the first in signals that the name lies within the next words

explanation.surface: A woman is in peril and facing danger.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across 'periL IN DAnger'.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Small twins, first pair to get lost

indicators.note: the first two letters of the twins word disappear

parts.note: Gemini is the star sign of the twins

explanation.surface: Little twins are told the first two of them will go missing.
explanation.walkthrough: GEMINI, the Twins of the zodiac, loses its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mini means very small, as in a miniature version.

clue.text: Church in which the French soldiers will be given money and fruit

indicators.note: in which says the following pieces sit inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
le is French for the
men are soldiers
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: French troops in a church are paid and fed.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is old British slang for money; 'will be given' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A clementine is a small citrus fruit like a tangerine.

clue.text: What may be found in school textbook, awful grey tome

definitions.text: What may be found in school textbook

indicators.note: awful means dreadful, so the letters are a mess and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dull schoolbook is described as a drab old volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges GREY TOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometry is a branch of mathematics studied from school textbooks.

clue.text: Old Greek graduate stuck within that time

indicators.note: stuck within means placed inside the word for that time

parts.note: then means at that time
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek scholar was stuck in his era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck within' places the graduate abbreviation inside the word for that time; Thebes was a leading city of ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A Theban was a citizen of Thebes, a city of ancient Greece.
